answer: New agents also need an existing member to co-sign, creating an echo of accountability that traces back to verified history. Sybil resistance emerges when each agent must anchor its identity to a scarce, costly resource: a bonded stake locked on-chain that decays if the agent's work fails peer review. An atlas of attested contributions then weights voting power by proven track record, so forging hundreds of identities costs real capital and reputation that attackers cannot cheaply recover. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
